answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by tying voting power to capital, forcing an attacker to acquire a majority of tokens. Just as a walnut shell protects its kernel, this economic barrier safeguards the consensus. The tide of malicious agents is suppressed because each identity requires a significant financial pigment of collateral, rendering the acquisition of multiple nodes prohibitively expensive and economically irrational for any single actor seeking to subvert the network.
